Experiments used to be expensive.Now they cost a weekend.

So I run a lot of them. Everything here is an idea I gave a night or two — substrates, frameworks, agent tools, products and design studies, most built solo in spare hours. The barrier to trying something didn't move. It disappeared.

The person behind the index

I build software that questions its own foundation.

I'm Chris Kluis. For nearly two decades I've worked the seam where product, marketing, and go-to-market meet in B2B SaaS — I took an enterprise software company from on-prem to SaaS to acquisition, and turned one too many "there has to be a better way" posts into co-founding SaaSRock. Back then I was the idea guy; a developer built everything.

So for years the deal was the same: dream it, write it up, hand it off. A new UX paradigm for relationship-aware data, APIs that could teach an LLM agent themselves — things I had no way to build myself. The tooling finally changed that. Everything here is me building the ideas I used to have to give away — and an open invitation for every other idea person to start experimenting too.

18+ yrs B2B SaaS30% → 80% ARR1 acquisitionCo-founded SaaSRockPalm Harbor, FL

Foundations

What if the layer under everything were different?

Substrates, kernels and languages — the floor a product stands on, rebuilt from first principles to see what changes above it.

    regel

    What if deploying were a commit, and rolling back were a WHERE clause?

    A Go kernel runs strict-TypeScript apps admitted as content-addressed Postgres rows. Deploy is a commit; rollback is an as-of WHERE clause — and nothing lands unverified.

  4. 01.04 tinkerinternal tools on data you can't see Shipped ↗
    Shipped01.04 · Foundations

    tinker

    What if you could build internal tools on personal data nobody can read without a second person's approval?

    An ontology-driven builder in Rust on PostgreSQL 18. Define an object once and get a row-level-secured table, a governed API and an MCP front door for agents. Email and phone are sealed by type in a separate vault: queries see a mask, automations get a key, and a person sees the value only after a second person approves. Erasure is a crypto-shred.

    662tests passing
    M0–M8gated milestones
    RustPostgreSQL 18MCP
    Live ↗Code ↗

Group 03 · 4 experiments

Agent tools

Making agents cheaper, better reviewed, and easier to steer.

Orchestrators, review frameworks and native tools for working with AI agents every day — measured, routed and reviewed.

4 shipped
  1. 03.01 batonv3.1an orchestrator of orchestrators Shipped ↗
    Shipped03.01 · Agent tools

    batonv3.1

    What if every task went to the cheapest model that could actually finish it?

    An orchestrator of orchestrators, routed by what it costs. Say what you want and it picks a mode, plans a graph, and sends every task to the cheapest rung that can finish it — escalating one rung at a time, asking before it spends the expensive one, and handing you a one-slide brief at each decision instead of a report to dig through.

    6rungs
    10modes
    44personas
    40experts
    PromptsMulti-agentClaude
    Live ↗Code ↗v2 ↗v1 ↗

    Shipped03.02 · Agent tools

    luminaryTeam

    What would 40 domain experts find if they reviewed your plan before launch?

    A multi-agent technical review framework — drop in a codebase, spec, or launch plan and get an adversarial audit from 40 domain experts across 7 phases, synthesized into ranked fixes.

    PromptsMulti-agentClaude
    Live ↗Code ↗
  3. 03.03 senkanitoken compression for coding agents Shipped ↗
    Shipped03.03 · Agent tools

    senkani

    How many tokens could a coding agent skip if every read were compressed before it arrived?

    Token compression for AI coding agents — a native macOS binary that compresses every file read and filters shell output from a local index before a token reaches Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP agent.

    SwiftmacOSMCP
    Live ↗Code ↗
  4. 03.04 workflowForgepaste a workflow, get a page you can send Shipped ↗
    Shipped03.04 · Agent tools

    workflowForge

    What if any workflow could become a diagram you can send — one where no two lines ever cross?

    Paste a workflow, get a page you can send. Whatever model you already use writes the JSON; one self-contained HTML file draws it as a DRAKON-style diagram — happy path down the left, exceptions fanning right, severity by shape, and no two lines ever cross. Every step carries a verified, disputed, or unverified state only a human can advance, and the page never reads your process.

    Single-file HTMLSVG rendererBring your own modelNo server
    Live ↗Code ↗

How this page is built

29 folders. One registry. One page.

Every experiment is a folder with its own item.json and preview. A zero-dependency script reads them into registry.json and writes this page, the README table and the counts. Adding an experiment is adding a folder.
